review_purpose: Review R782 and R783 decision-support reports for scope, depth, novelty, source precision, license and reuse limits; pin all inputs and provide section-limited retrieval metadata and eligible future scopes. Read-only review only. No Git, source edits, builds, tests, GPU/profiler work, process inspection, cleanup, or independent external-source verification was performed.

research_index.note: The reports array ends at R780 and does not yet contain R782 or R783. This reviewer did not edit the index.

reports.scope_depth_review: Within its 1,400–1,900-word budget and six listed primary-source families, below the seven-source limit. It supplies the requested contract table, explains separate HC/residual, coefficient, norm, and recurrent-state boundaries, maps the contracts to Strata, and gives a bounded component experiment with explicit limitations. R782 is meaningfully complementary to R783: framework producer/consumer and state contracts rather than Intel kernel/API alternatives.
reports.source_precision: The report pins vLLM and SGLang to exact 40-character commits, identifies paths and symbols for the described boundaries, and records repository licenses plus the per-file MIT provenance of the vendored FLA recurrent source. No source was reused. This reviewer did not independently verify the cited files.
reports.reuse_and_evidence_limits: Framework contracts are design references, not transferable Strata invariants or Intel SYCL performance evidence. The report explicitly distinguishes persistent state from activation storage, preserves FP32 accumulation/router/recurrent state, and says the physical-byte arithmetic is not a speed or fit prediction. Treat all external kernels as read-only references; any future reuse needs separate per-file provenance and license review.

reports.scope_depth_review: Within its 1,400–1,900-word budget and six substantive source-family limit. It compares a concrete Strata GEMM-to-SwiGLU seam, grouped GEMM, oneMKL output signatures, ESIMD and owned joint_matrix; distinguishes API output types from proven accumulator types; and gives a bounded experiment with exact limitations. The owned-kernel and framework-contract angles add useful implementation detail beyond R782.
reports.source_precision: Paths, functions and Strata call-site line numbers are specific, but the report itself says its vLLM-XPU, LLM Scaler and Intel LLVM URLs use mutable main/sycl branches and provides no immutable source revisions. Intel oneMKL's URL is versioned; the B570 product page and issue #22926 identify supporting context. The reported Strata line locations belong to an unpinned read-only source snapshot and should be checked against the live feature/sycl tree. No source was independently verified in this review.
reports.license_and_reuse_limits: The report correctly flags the BSD-3-Clause notice on the cited vLLM-XPU interface despite the repository's Apache-2.0 root license, and identifies LLM Scaler's Apache-2.0 context. It proposes no adoption. The owned joint_matrix approach is a design recommendation; do not copy third-party code or treat this review as license clearance. Any future adaptation needs an immutable source pin and complete notice review under the repository MIT policy.
reports.main_correction_to_retain: Its recommended first prototype is FP16 MoE gate/up output, whereas Main's current implementation is BF16 hidden/residual storage and BF16 GEMM outputs. Do not transfer the report's FP16 choice to that work. It expressly says BF16 needs a separate input/weight representation decision, and the matrix tuple must be queried on the exact runtime/device. The report establishes no B570 performance, model quality, or active compiler support.

cross_report_assessment.novelty_and_redundancy: Both reports address the current native-16 producer/consumer request, so they overlap in typed-output terminology. Their investigations remain distinct: R782 maps mHC/GDN activation and persistent-state contracts across vLLM/SGLang; R783 traces Intel-oriented GEMM choices and a concrete MoE consumer seam. Together they cover the requested task without becoming duplicate source surveys.
cross_report_assessment.applicability_and_evidence_limits: Both are source-level decision support only. Neither ran Strata, measured B570 performance, established 256K quality, or verified the active toolchain's matrix tuple. R782's immutable framework commits make its referenced contract locations retrievable. R783's mutable project-branch links weaken later reproducibility; re-pin exact files before any implementation reuse. The current index predates both reports, so its index entry remains outstanding.
cross_report_assessment.main_correction_to_retain: For the active BF16 path, R782's storage-versus-accumulation boundaries apply directly. From R783, retrieve only the GEMM seam and owned joint_matrix sections plus the exact-device capability caveat. Its FP16 GU recommendation is a separate candidate and is not evidence to choose FP16 for BF16 residuals. Verify live Strata call sites and runtime matrix combinations independently.
cross_report_assessment.outcome: Both reports are substantive, within scope and useful for the present implementation with section-limited retrieval. No report body needs to be summarized or copied into product files.
